role: Acceptance check of the bwx12 kernel machine code, run after the build.
purpose: The script reads the objdump text of the 55 kernels of `bwx12` (`listing.txt`) and the table of loop addresses (`offsets.tsv`). It accepts the build only when the 29 kernels of the earlier runner `bwx11` are unchanged and the 26 new kernels have exactly the planned instructions and loop position.

main_flow.step: When Python loads the file, it builds the table `NEW`: the expected loop of each of the 26 new kernels.
`main` reads the arguments: the listing, the offsets table and the options.
It reads the reference listing, the new listing and both offsets tables. It ends with exit status 2 when a file is unusable.
Part 1: for each of the 29 kernels of the reference it compares the function text without addresses and the loop start modulo 64. It prints one row per kernel.
It checks the places of the table of global addresses over all kernels. It rejects a kernel that neither the reference nor `NEW` holds.
Part 2: for each of the 26 new kernels it applies the five rules of `new_problems`. It prints one row per kernel.
It prints the summary line. It returns 0 when no check failed, and 1 when a check failed.

behavior_notes: The scripts of the whole-chip test (`go.sh`, `go2.sh`, `ra.sh`, `rx.sh`) do not call this script. It ran after the build of `bwx12` on 2026-11-15, and the test of 2026-11-17 used the binary of that build [Ref4] [Ref5].

The output for that build is saved in the file `check_listing12.out` in the build folder `crb-build-1` [Ref1]. All 29 rows of part 1 say `same` and `ok`. All 26 rows of part 2 say `expected` and `ok`. The summary line reports 0 failed rows in both parts.

In this task (2026-11-21) the script was run again on the same `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv`. It printed the same 58 lines as the saved output and ended with exit status 0. The saved output file has the modification time 2026-11-15 17:12:22 UTC on the development machine. The build on CRB ended at 17:12:14 UTC by the clock of CRB [Ref4]. Insufficient data: the command line that wrote the saved output file on 2026-11-15. A shell history or a session log of that day would resolve it.

Part 1 passed for five kernels of the whole-chip test: `oldread` (the old read kernel), `read` (the new read kernel), `asmread`, `read_nop96` and `read_1pl` [Ref1]. This proves that every instruction of each function in `bwx12`, with every operand, equals the instruction at the same position in the accepted build of `bwx11`. Addresses are excluded from the comparison in the way that lines 27 to 42 define.

Proved for the same five kernels: the loop start modulo 64 equals the value of `bwx11`. The values are 40 bytes for `oldread`, 36 bytes for `read`, and 20 bytes for `asmread`, `read_nop96` and `read_1pl` [Ref1].

Part 2 passed for `read_nop256`. This proves that the loop is exactly the 8 `ldp` of `asmread` (256 bytes loaded per loop pass), then 256 `nop`, then `add x0, x0, #0x100`, `cmp x0, x1` and a `b.cc` back to the loop start. No instruction of the loop uses a loaded value. The function has no other branch or call. It stores d8 to d15 before the loop and reloads them after it. Its loop start modulo 64 is 20 bytes, the value of `asmread` in the same listing [Ref1].

Limit: for the 29 kernels of part 1 the script proves equality with `bwx11` only. It holds no expected instruction list for them. The instructions of the old and the new read kernel are in the blocks `oldread` and `read` of `listing.txt` [Ref2].
Limit: the script does not compare `bwx12` with `bw_old` or `bw_new`. It reads no listing of these two binaries.

Limit: the script checks kernel functions only. It does not check the code that times a kernel. The whole-chip test uses the interval mode of `bwx12` [Ref11]. In this mode the function `worker` of `bwx12.c` reads the clock, and it calls each kernel through the function `call` [Ref10]. No file in the build folder `crb-build-1` holds the machine code of `worker` or `call`. The file `seq-listing.txt` lists `timed_sequence` and `timed_sequence_hot`. These two functions read the clock in the trial mode only, and the whole-chip test does not use the trial mode [Ref10]. `build12.sh` says that no script uses `seq-listing.txt` [Ref6].

Limit: the script reads no digest. `build.txt` records the sha256 values of the binary `bwx12`, of `listing.txt` and of `offsets.tsv` from one build [Ref4]. The files `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv` in the build folder have the recorded values (computed in this task). The binary `bwx12` is not in the local folders. So its sha256 value is known from the records only. `go.sh` stops unless the binary has the recorded value [Ref5].
The script writes no file. It prints its tables to standard output. Exit status: 0 all checks passed, 1 a check failed, 2 a file could not be used or the arguments are wrong.

words.def: the Arm reference server under test. It has 128 CPUs.
the two halves of the chip. CPUs 0-63 sit on mesh 0. CPUs 64-127 sit on mesh 1.
our runs use CPUs 0-119 only: 64 threads on mesh 0 plus 56 threads on mesh 1. Each thread reads its own buffer of 256 MiB from memory.
the run of 2026-11-17 on the whole chip. Of `bwx12` it ran six kernels: `oldread`, `read`, `asmread`, `read_nop96`, `read_nop256` and `read_1pl`.
one loop function of the benchmark: a read, a write or a copy loop. Its function name in the binary is `k_` plus the kernel name. The operating system kernel is always written "Linux kernel".
the inner loop of the benchmark that reads memory.
portable C code with 16 running sums. Each load is followed by an add. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_old and `oldread` in the runner bwx12.
NEON intrinsics (C functions that map to Arm vector instructions), loads only. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_new and `read` in bwx12.
a hand-written load-only loop. It has the same 8 "ldp q" loads per 256 B as the new read kernel. "ldp q" is the Arm instruction that loads two 16-byte vector registers.
test loops of bwx12: the asmread loop with 96 or 256 no-operation instructions per 256 B, and a loop with one load per 64 B line.
the benchmark and its two binaries of 2026-11-13. bw_old was built from the old source, bw_new from the new source.
later runner programs for the same loops. They print one row per thread. bwx12 is the runner of the 2026-11-15 investigation. bwx11 and bwx are older versions.

the two modes of `bwx12`. Interval mode (option `--seq`): every thread runs a sequence of kernels. In one timed interval a thread calls one kernel only, one or more times. The whole-chip test uses it. Trial mode (option `--trial`): one thread runs the trials of a plan file. The whole-chip test does not use it.
the machine on which this script ran. It is not CRB. The file `test_kernels12.py` in the same folder describes it as x86-64.
the 64-bit Arm instruction set. The listing of the CRB build is AArch64 code.
the Python type `dict`: a table from keys to values.
a tool that prints the machine code of a binary as text: one instruction per line, with its address.
the objdump text of every kernel function of `bwx12`, written by `build12.sh` on CRB. The block of one kernel starts with a line `=== bwx12 <kernel> ===`.
a table with one row per kernel, written by `build12.sh` on CRB. Its columns are `binary`, `kernel`, `function`, `start`, `loop_start` and `loop_mod64`.
the `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv` of the accepted build of `bwx11`, saved in the folder `ref-bwx11`.
a build of a runner whose listing passed its checker script. For `bwx12` it is the build whose files are saved in the folder `crb-build-1`.
the name in `bwx12.c` for the 26 kernels that `bwx12` adds to `bwx11`. It is not a round of a kernel sequence.
a branch instruction whose target address is lower than its own address.
the loop of a function is the range from the target of its first backward branch to that branch. The loop start is the address of the first instruction of this range.
the remainder of the loop start address divided by 64. It gives the position of the loop start inside a 64-byte block of code. The value is a number of bytes from 0 to 63.

three names for the 32 vector registers of AArch64. `qN` is the full 16-byte register N. `dN` is its low 8 bytes. `vN.2d` is the register as two 64-bit lanes. A lane is one element of a vector register.
`ldp` loads a pair of registers from memory. `stp` stores a pair. `ldr` loads one register.
an instruction that does nothing.
two names of one conditional branch. After `cmp a, b` it jumps when a is below b as unsigned numbers.
`bl` calls a function. `ret` returns to the caller.
an instruction that puts the address of a 4096-byte page into a register.
`movi` sets every lane of a vector register to a constant. `dup` copies a general register into every lane of a vector register.
a table in the binary that holds addresses of global objects. Code reads an entry with `adrp` plus `ldr`. In the function `whole` the list of the used entries has the name `got`.
a value that the compiler puts on the stack at function entry and compares before the return. When the value changed, the function calls `__stack_chk_fail`.
a register that must hold the same value when a function returns as when it was called. For v8 to v15 this holds for the low 8 bytes, the registers d8 to d15.
a plain C loop that replaces an assembly kernel when the build machine is not AArch64.
a digest: a value of 64 hexadecimal digits computed from the bytes of a file. Files with equal sha256 values are taken as equal.

functions.name: vadd
functions.what: Builds the text of vector add instructions from pairs of register numbers.

functions.name: spec
functions.what: Returns the expectation of one new kernel: loop instructions, planned loop start modulo 64, original kernel, instructions before the loop, end-pointer instruction.

functions.name: sections
functions.what: Reads a listing file into a dictionary from (binary, kernel) to the list of (address, instruction text).

functions.name: offsets
functions.what: Reads `offsets.tsv` into a dictionary from (binary, kernel) to the text of column `loop_mod64`. Raises `ValueError` on a wrong header or row.

functions.name: loop_start
functions.what: Returns the target address of the first backward branch inside the function, or `None`.

functions.name: whole
functions.what: Returns the function text with addresses removed, and the places of the pointer loads from the table of global addresses.

functions.name: numbers
functions.what: Returns the register numbers that one `SAVE` or `RESTORE` match captured.

functions.name: new_problems
functions.what: Applies the five rules of part 2 to one new kernel and returns the list of problems.

functions.name: main
functions.what: Parses the arguments, reads the files, runs part 1 and part 2, prints one row per kernel, returns the exit status.

refs.what: the saved output of this script for the build in `crb-build-1`. Lines 2 to 30 are the 29 rows of part 1. Lines 32 to 57 are the 26 rows of part 2. Line 58 is the summary line.

the checked listing. The blocks of the six kernels of the whole-chip test start at these lines: `read` 1, `asmread` 59, `oldread` 133, `read_1pl` 754, `read_nop96` 854, `read_nop256` 2126. The `adrp` and `bl` instructions are at lines 137, 189, 204, 313, 365 and 380.

the reference files `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv`. A `cmp` in this task found them equal to the two files in `/home/jhan/workspace/titan/cache-perf/crb/tmp/agent-scratch/bwx11-2026-11-15/crb-build-1/`. The `adrp` instructions of the reference listing are at lines 137, 189, 313 and 365.
lines 20 to 22 hold the sha256 values of `bwx12`, `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv`. Line 24 holds the end time of the build, 2026-11-15T17:12:14Z.

line 13 holds the sha256 value of `bwx12` that line 20 of `build.txt` records. Line 23 stops the driver when the binary has another value. `go2.sh` in the same folder holds the same value in line 10 and makes the same check in line 19.
lines 57 to 75 write `listing.txt` and `offsets.tsv`. Line 21 says that no script uses `seq-listing.txt`. Line 22 names this script as the next step.
lines 3 to 11 and line 1080: `bwx12.c` is `bwx11.c` plus the additions of round 5. The additions are 26 kernels.
line 141, section "Fixed setup": the design rule that a build is rejected when its acceptance listing differs. Lines 2 and 3 of the script cite it.
lines 605 to 641, macro `DEF_ASMREAD`: a kernel takes a pointer and a count of 8-byte words. The list of changed registers makes gcc save d8 to d15 outside the loop.

lines 90 to 94 name the two modes: `--seq` for the interval mode, `--trial` for the trial mode. Lines 2913 and 2914 send a command line with `--trial` to `trial_main`. Function `worker` (from line 1632) is the thread of the interval mode: with the option `--stop common` of the whole-chip test it reads the start time of an interval in line 1688. It calls the kernel through `call` in line 1695 and reads the clock after each call in line 1700. The last of these clock reads is the end time of the interval. Line 1491 defines `call`. Lines 1995 and 2056 define `timed_sequence` and `timed_sequence_hot`. Their only calls are in lines 2206 and 2209, in the function `run_trial` of the trial mode.

the files `like.spec`, `cfwd.spec` and `crev.spec` hold the arguments of the `bwx12` processes of the whole-chip test. Each one has `--seq` and no `--trial`. Together the three `--seq` lists name the six kernels `oldread`, `read`, `asmread`, `read_nop96`, `read_nop256` and `read_1pl`.
